# Independent audit and exact failure of the asymmetric scalar criterion



## 1. Audit of the adjacent-layer results

For centrally symmetric endpoints about a common origin, the common intersection contributes exactly its entire mass to a pair of opposite scalar thresholds. The two nonnegative residual measures remain symmetric even when their supports are nonconvex. One threshold is nonpositive, so the corresponding residual contributes at least half its mass. This proves the claimed endpoint-pair lower bound. Closed supporting boundaries have zero full-dimensional volume, and vertical caps capture an entire endpoint.

For crossed rectangles, the two displayed fixed caps cover the entire real middle plane and have exactly the asserted masses. Their supporting traces on the short side have zero area. Thus the all-center upper bound is independent of any minimizer or stationarity assumption, and matches the common-intersection lower bound.

When the endpoints are moved to bases \(-1,1\), the forced middle square has the stated side length. Each proper cap through its center takes exactly half its area. The endpoint-pair lower bound and the two fixed covering caps again coincide. Vertical caps have larger mass. At the exposed endpoint bases, a steep tilt isolates any chosen own-fiber cap, so the endpoint maxima are exactly their ordinary symmetric half-volume depths. The claimed global three-fiber maximum follows.

The asymmetric Section 4 estimate correctly keeps three distinct available centers: an ordinary middle center, the larger endpoint center, and the origin in the forced symmetric midpoint body. It does not assume that the arbitrary actual middle body is symmetric. Its vertical-cap check uses \(I\le a\) and \(w\le U\) in the correct direction. The subsequent scalar criterion is sufficient, and the optimization over unrestricted \(U>0\) is correctly separated from geometric realizability.

## 2. The requested scalar inequality is already false for intervals

Let \(\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d\). For centrally symmetric convex bodies \(A,C\), write

\[
a=|A|\le b=|C|,\quad
w=|(A+C)/2|,\quad I=|A\cap C|.
\]

The proposed universal inequality is

\[
\max\{b,w+a+I\}\ \ge\ 2\Gamma_d(a+b).
\tag{1}
\]

In dimension one take the exact centered intervals

\[
C=[-1/2,1/2],\qquad A=[-1/10,1/10].
\]

They have

\[
b=1,\qquad a=I=1/5,\qquad w=3/5.
\]

Consequently the left side of (1) is exactly \(1\), while the right side is \(6/5\). This is a strict gap of \(1/5\), with no limiting or numerical argument.

More generally, for \(C=[-1/2,1/2]\) and \(A=tC\), \(0<t\le1\), the exact shortfall of (1) is

\[
\Delta(t)=1+t-\max\{1,(1+5t)/2\}
=
\begin{cases}
t,&0<t\le1/5,\\
(1-3t)/2,&1/5\le t\le1.
\end{cases}
\]

Thus failure occurs for every \(0<t<1/3\), with maximum shortfall \(1/5\) at \(t=1/5\).

## 3. Exact planar failure and the unresolved estimate window

For a dimension-at-least-two certificate, take

\[
C=[-1/2,1/2]^2,\qquad A=\tfrac12 C.
\]

Then

\[
b=1,\quad a=I=1/4,\quad w=9/16,
\]

and

\[
\max\{b,w+a+I\}=17/16<10/9=2\Gamma_2(a+b),
\]

with exact gap \(7/144\).

In the source's notation \(K=\max\{b,w+a+I\}/2=17/32\). Using only its two bounds \(\max\{\Gamma_2U,K\}\), the desired three-fiber target is not reached for

\[
73/64<U<5/4.
\]

The worst normalized estimate occurs at \(U=K/\Gamma_2=153/128\). These are statements about the insufficiency of those lower bounds, not upper bounds on actual depth.

Neither nested-interval nor homothetic-square construction disproves OC. They rule out the specific proposed scalar compensation inequality and show that any further three-fiber argument needs additional cap information beyond \(b,w,a,I\) combined in (1).
